questions.work: Put t = x² + 1, dt = 2x dx: ½∫₁² dt/t = ½(log 2 − log 1) = ½ log 2.
The integrand changes sign when x → −x: it is odd, so the integral over [−a, a] is 0.
I = ∫ sin³x/(sin³x + cos³x) dx too (x → π/2 − x). Adding: 2I = π/2 ⇒ I = π/4.

questions.q: True or False: (a) ∫₂³ 3ˣ dx = 18. (b) ∫_(−½)^(½) cos x log((1 + x)/(1 − x)) dx = 1.
questions.answer:
(a) False — [3ˣ/log 3]₂³ = (27 − 9)/log 3 = 18/log 3.
(b) False — cos x is even and log((1 + x)/(1 − x)) is odd, so the product is odd and the integral is 0.

questions.q: Evaluate ∫₀^(π/2) (sin x − cos x)/(1 + sin x cos x) dx.
questions.answer:
Replace x by π/2 − x: I = ∫₀^(π/2) (cos x − sin x)/(1 + sin x cos x) dx = −I.
So 2I = 0 ⇒ I = 0.

I = ∫ √cos x/(√cos x + √sin x) dx. Replacing x by π/2 − x (which keeps the limits π/6, π/3) gives I = ∫ √sin x/(√sin x + √cos x) dx.
Adding: 2I = ∫_(π/6)^(π/3) dx = π/6 ⇒ I = π/12.

questions.q: Prove that y² = 4x and x² = 4y divide the square bounded by x = 0, x = 4, y = 4 and y = 0 into three equal parts.
questions.answer:
The curves meet at (0, 0) and (4, 4).
Middle part: ∫₀⁴ (2√x − x²/4)dx = [(4/3)x^(3/2) − x³/12]₀⁴ = 32/3 − 16/3 = 16/3.
Lower part (under x² = 4y): ∫₀⁴ x²/4 dx = 16/3.
Upper part = 16 − 16/3 − 16/3 = 16/3. All three are equal.

or.q: Find the area of the smaller region bounded by x²/a² + y²/b² = 1 and x/a + y/b = 1.
or.answer:
Quarter ellipse area = πab/4. Triangle under the line from (a, 0) to (0, b) has area ab/2.
Smaller region = πab/4 − ab/2 = (π − 2)ab/4.

questions.q: Find the smaller area enclosed by the circle x² + y² = 4 and the line x + y = 2.
questions.answer:
The line meets the circle at (2, 0) and (0, 2).
Area = ∫₀² [√(4 − x²) − (2 − x)]dx = [quarter circle] − [triangle] = π − 2.
